pageProps.title: The 11-Character Murder
pageProps.review: A book review of Keigo Higashino's novel that densely deals with realistic groups of people where there is no absolute good or evil and the moral dilemma of true justice through the alternating perspectives of the protagonist and the culprit.
pageProps.description: The echo of resentment that rang from a deserted island
pageProps.content:
## Review The entire work seems to be constructed based on the theme: ```There is not a single good person in this murder```. The author does not apply an absolute yardstick of good or evil to any of the characters. This would be a more realistic character setting.
Instead of asking ```who is the worst```, it gives a fundamental moral dilemma of what is true justice.
By narrating with alternating perspectives of the protagonist and the culprit, one can better feel the agony and determination within the culprit's heart.
For me, the culprit's motive is somewhat difficult to understand.
